answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol routes identity verification through an economic prism where each additional clone incurs superlinear quadratic stake burning. Like shifting sand across a barren dune, forged nodes face exponential slashing if they wander from verified operational topologies. Attackers face an aggregate cost scaling as O(N^2) relative to honest participants, creating deterministic economic friction that renders mass identity generation mathematically unviable.
